  "limitations_stated": [
    "Discordance between animal and human studies may be due to bias or to the failure of animal models to mimic clinical disease adequately.",
    "Animal studies are often carried out to learn about biological mechanisms and we cannot comment on the value of animal research in these areas nor provide precise estimates of agreement.",
    "We analysed what was reported and cannot rule out that other relevant data were not published.",
    "The animal studies varied in methodological quality and sample sizes rather than providing a single definitive high quality experiment for each intervention.",
    "Randomisation and blinding were rarely reported, which can have important implications as it has been shown that animal experiments carried out without either are five times more likely to report a positive treatment effect.",
    "The number of experiments in the other systematic reviews made assessment of publication bias difficult.",
    "Given the extent of heterogeneity, the precision of pooled results is open to question.",
    "The usefulness of animal testing has, however, been questioned.",
    "Some believe that the results from animal experiments cannot be applied to humans because of the biological differences between the species and because the results of animal experiments often depend on the type of animal model.",
    "The quality of the experiments was poor.",
    "The funnel plot suggested an excess of imprecise studies overstating efficacy.",
    "The funnel plot suggested a preponderance of small experiments overstating efficacy but this was not supported by an Egger regression analysis.",
    "The data were sparse for antenatal corticosteroids and mortality.",
    "All experiments for bisphosphonates were carried out in ovariectomised animals.",
    "The animal models for head injury where there were differences in the results, seemed less representative of the condition in humans than the animal models for stroke.",
    "In head injury, treatment was given within five minutes of injury in the animal models but up to eight hours after injury in the clinical trials.",
    "None of the animal experiments used models that mimic the complex situations that usually follow traumatic head injury.",
    "Comorbidities were examined in the stroke models but not in the head injury models.",
    "There is a gap between clinical research and clinical practice.",
    "There is a lack of communication between those involved in animal research and clinical trialists."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "IR was an investigator in the corticosteroid randomisation after significant head injury trial. The trial was funded by the UK Medical Research Council. Pharmacia and Upjohn (Pfizer from 2003) provided the Medical Research Council with the methylprednisolone (free of charge) needed for the trial, a grant in aid for preparation of the placebo, and support for collaborators’ meetings. PS is co-chief investigator of the third international stroke trial, testing intravenous recombinant tissue plasminogen activator in acute ischaemic stroke; the start-up phase (completed in 2005) of this trial was supported by Boehringer Ingelheim, the manufacturers of tissue plasminogen activator, a donation of drug and placebo for the first 300 patients. The current phase of the trial is supported by the Medical Research Council and the Health Foundation. None of the authors have any relevant competing financial interests.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "pooled odds ratio for adverse functional outcome 0.58 (95% confidence interval 0.41 to 0.83) for corticosteroids in animal models of head injury",
    "tissue plasminogen activator reduced infarct volume by 24% (95% confidence interval 20% to 28%) in animal models of stroke",
    "tissue plasminogen activator improved neurobehavioural scores by 23% (17% to 29%) in animal models of stroke",
    "tissue plasminogen activator increased the probability of haemorrhage (odds ratio 1.96, 95% confidence interval 1.63 to 2.35) in animal models of stroke",
    "tirilazad reduced infarct volume by 29% (95% confidence interval 21% to 37%) in animal models of stroke",
    "tirilazad improved neurobehavioural scores by 48% (29% to 67%) in animal models of stroke",
    "pooled odds ratio for mortality 4.2 (95% confidence interval 0.85 to 20.9) for antenatal corticosteroids in animal models",
    "pooled odds ratio for mortality in ewe models was 12.5 (1.9 to 79.2) for antenatal corticosteroids",
    "alendronate increased bone mineral density by 11.0% (95% confidence interval 9.2% to 12.9%) in the combined results for the hip region in animal models",
    "treatment effect in the lumbar spine was 8.5% (5.8% to 11.2%) for alendronate in animal models",
    "treatment effect in the combined results for the forearms (baboons only) was 1.7% ( − 1.4% to 4.7%) for alendronate in animal models",
    "animal experiments carried out without either [randomisation or blinding] are five times more likely to report a positive treatment effect"
